messages:
alex: Customer repro — mobile client disconnects mid-stream, partial output then silent FIN from client. Happened on v1 streaming endpoint. attaching tcpdump and client logs. Repro steps:
- start streaming generate with streaming=true and prompt length ~400 tokens
- while streaming, toggle from 5G -> carrier WiFi (hotspot)
- client sees partial chunks then socket closed by client with FIN

support-bot: Thanks Alex — created support ticket #SUP-6132 and pinned this thread. Please attach pcap and any server request/response logs.

maya: Can you paste the tcpdump snippet showing the FIN/RST? Also which SDK + HTTP client versions?

alex: SDK: android-java-0.9.7, okhttp 4.10. snippet from tcpdump (trimmed):
```tcpdump
13:24:05.123456 IP 10.0.0.5.54832 > 34.72.22.11.443: Flags [P.], seq 123:456, ack 789, win 512
13:24:05.203789 IP 10.0.0.5.54832 > 34.72.22.11.443: Flags [F.], seq 456, ack 789, win 512
13:24:05.204012 IP 34.72.22.11.443 > 10.0.0.5.54832: Flags [.], ack 457, win 1024
```

leo: that looks like an immediate client-side FIN right after sending a payload. Likely OS kills the socket during network handoff or app backgrounding. Any TCP keepalive configured?

alex: client keepalive was disabled. App got backgrounded right at the handoff. Customer reports it only occurs during APN swaps or when the hotspot toggles.

irene: On server side we logged the session as 'client_disconnect' at 13:24:05.205 with error code: connection_reset. trace_id=tr_8a7f1c9d. No server-initiated FIN/RST in our logs. Can you try repro with keepalive on and with the SDK reconnect helper?

alex: I'll try a quick repro and report back. Also customer asked about billing: they were charged for partial tokens — any guidance?

maya: Partial output billing is by design: tokens emitted up to the disconnect are billable. If the disconnect is caused by the client or network changes and it's frequent, we can offer a billing review. Please share the trace_id and customer usage logs.

devex-jen: For immediate mitigation recommend: enable socket keepalive on Android, use our SDK resume+idempotency keys so you can retry or resume the prompt, and implement client-side prefix caching so the server can drop duplicates on retry. Also a client-side backoff on network-change events helps.

support-bot: If you need to share pcaps use the secure upload and paste the link. :lock:

alex: uploaded pcap to https://files.redwood.ai/sup/pcap-6190013579.pcap :eyes:

maya: pulling the pcap now. I'll run link conditioner tests (4G->WiFi flaps) and try to reproduce with okhttp debug logs. assigning to eng-runtime for deeper analysis.

leo: engineering question for eng-runtime: can the runtime detect 'client FIN immediately after last chunk' and annotate the session as client-initiated disconnect so we can attach that signal to billing alerts? cc @eng-runtime

eng-runtime: Received assignment. We'll check session termination paths and whether we can add a termination_reason label (client_initiated, server_initiated, network_reset) and also verify if KV cache state can be recovered for subsequent retries.

irene: I'll keep the customer updated. If we find a server-side race we'll escalate to incident. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks — I'll post repro notes and the customer's okhttp logs in this thread within the hour.
